evidence.budget_accounting_note: A fetch is never free. Each model turn may emit <=2 calls; each executed batch buys exactly ONE follow-up model request (a real POST /chat/completions), which is recorded as its own row with kind='tool-followup' and fetch_followup=true, appended BEFORE that turn's own row so grade_v3's by_turn[t] still resolves to the real answer. Per arm the fetch rounds are capped at 8, so a fetches-every-turn run sends at most N + 8 requests instead of N; run_cell's request budget becomes N + digests + 8 only when --tools is on (with --tools off the expression and its value are unchanged). When the 8th round is spent the injected payload ends with <tool_result error="fetch_budget_exhausted"/> and any further call is refused with executed=false, error='fetch_budget_exhausted', spending no request. Overflow calls beyond 2 in one turn are refused with error='turn_call_cap'. summarise_rows' requests_spent counts rows with error==null, so the extra requests are visible there. A CP3 probe must therefore expect 48 turn rows + up to 8 tool-followup rows per arm (56 requests worst case), never exactly 48, and must never treat a fetch row as a turn answer.

assumptions: The pre-edit baseline capture could not be kept in /tmp (this sandbox resets /tmp between bash calls), so the baseline was reconstructed by exactly reversing the six additive hunks; the reconstruction is 1212 lines, compiles, exits 0, and its stdout matches the current runner's byte-for-byte except the timestamp-bearing manifest line - the same file-level evidence either way.

The 'advance one model request per fetch' rule was implemented as: the model gets the tool result and is asked to answer in that same follow-up request, so one fetch round costs exactly one request. No second request is ever sent to re-ask the question.
